explain.say: A sewing machine needle has its eye near the point. It never passes right through the cloth. Instead it pushes the top thread down through the fabric.

faq.a: The bobbin is a small spool under the needle plate holding the lower thread. Each loop of top thread is wrapped round it, so the two threads lock together.
asks: Why does a sewing machine need two threads?

faq.q: What does the hook do in a sewing machine?
faq.a: The hook spins below the fabric, catches the loop of top thread made by the needle and carries it round the bobbin to form the stitch.
asks: How does a sewing machine stitch?

faq.q: How can a needle sew without going all the way through?
faq.a: The eye is at the point, so the needle only needs to push a loop of thread under the cloth. The hook and bobbin do the rest underneath.
asks: Why is the hole at the tip of a sewing machine needle?

faq.a: Feed dogs are small toothed bars under the needle plate. Between stitches they rise, grip the cloth, move it a stitch length forward and drop again.
asks: How does the fabric move by itself?

faq.q: Why does thread bunch up underneath?
faq.a: Usually the top thread is not tight enough or is threaded wrongly, so loops are not pulled up. Rethreading with the presser foot up often fixes it.
asks: Why is my sewing machine making loops under the fabric?

facts: Elias Howe received a US patent for a lockstitch sewing machine in 1846.
A lockstitch interlocks a top thread and a bobbin thread in the middle of the fabric.

quiz.say: Where do the two threads of a lockstitch lock together?
quiz.show: Where do the two threads of a lockstitch lock together?

options.show: In the middle of the fabric
options.say: In the middle of the fabric

quiz.why: The take-up lever pulls the interlock up into the middle of the layers, so the stitch looks the same on both sides.

wrong.1: If the lock showed on top, the tension would be wrong.
wrong.2: The needle only carries the top thread; it does not hold the lock.
